top_stories.title: Over 41,000 DHS Employee Records Leaked Online
top_stories.summary: Over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employee records have been leaked online, allegedly stolen from an Okta single sign-on system. The breach exposed both personal and work information of DHS employees.

top_stories.title: DHS: 41,000+ Employee Records Leaked Online, Along With a Map of What Each Account Can Open
top_stories.summary: A threat actor has leaked a database containing personal and work details of more than 41,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees. The leaked data reportedly includes a map of what each account can access, exposing access entitlements and authorization structures across DHS systems.

top_stories.title: Ransomware gang talked AI agents into doing much of its dirty work
top_stories.summary: The Aur0ra ransomware group (tracked as GOLD OGRE by Sophos) used AI agents via the Cursor AI coding assistant to automate network intrusion, including credential collection and privilege escalation to domain administrator access. Attackers provided the agents with VPN logins, proxy access, and targets, allowing the AI to autonomously map networks and move laterally through victim environments.

top_stories.title: Shufti ties AI agent actions to verified owners and permissions
top_stories.summary: Shufti has launched Know Your Agent (KYA), a verification solution designed to authenticate autonomous AI agents and bind their actions to verified human or business owners with defined permissions. The product addresses the identity and authorization challenge of agentic AI systems that can open accounts, place orders, and move funds, going beyond simple access token validation to establish accountability and scope of approved actions.

top_stories.title: Attackers Chain Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws to Gain Unauthenticated Root Access
top_stories.summary: CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirmed active exploitation in the wild. The flaws, including CVE-2026-111357 (CVSS 8.8), a missing authentication vulnerability, are being chained with a third flaw to achieve unauthenticated root access on affected systems.

news.title: The first ten lines of a command policy for AI coding agents
news.summary: KloudStax CTO Vinay Thakker outlines identity and access control principles for AI coding agents in a Help Net Security interview. He covers agent identity assignment, credential proxy pitfalls, command policy construction, and network-level controls to prevent data exfiltration via package installs.

news.title: Chainalysis Confirms Intrusion Into Internal Tools and Exposure of Customer Identity Data
news.summary: Chainalysis, a blockchain analysis firm, confirmed a cybersecurity incident in which an external actor accessed non-sensitive customer identity data through internal tools. The company stated that authentication credentials, session tokens, and investigation content were not compromised in the breach.

news.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
news.summary: SS7 and Diameter protocol vulnerabilities allow attackers to intercept SMS-based authentication codes, enabling bypass of SMS-based MFA without compromising the target device. The article explains how these signaling flaws exploit inter-network trust relationships, directly undermining a widely-used second authentication factor.

news.title: Okta jumps after-hours following tapped inclusion in the S&P 500
news.summary: Okta has been selected by S&P Dow Jones Indices to join the S&P 500 benchmark index. The announcement caused Okta shares to climb 2.1% in after-hours trading.

news.title: Okta Set to Join S&P 500; Others to Join S&P MidCap 400 and S&P SmallCap 600
news.summary: Okta Inc. is set to join the S&P 500 index, moving up from the S&P MidCap 400, effective prior to the opening of trading on November 4. This index inclusion reflects Okta's market capitalization growth and raises its profile among institutional investors.

news.title: Implement least-privilege access with designations in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio has introduced a feature called "designations," which are named permission sets enabling granular, least-privilege access control for project members. Administrators can use designations to define and assign specific permissions to users within SageMaker projects, aligning with least-privilege access principles.

news.title: $38.4 bn market cap: DHS Data leak details - Okta says its core systems not compromised | All you need about company
news.summary: A data leak allegedly exposing personal and job details of over 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees is under investigation, with Distributed Denial of Secrets claiming the data came through Okta. Okta has responded stating it found no evidence that its core systems were compromised in the incident.

news.title: Hackers steal and publish data on 41,000 Homeland Security workers
news.summary: A hacker group claims to have stolen and published data on 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees. The exposed data includes work contact details and internal group memberships, which are relevant to identity and access management concerns around personnel data and directory exposure.

news.title: Hackers leak personnel data of 41,000+ Homeland Security staff, including ICE and border agents
news.summary: Hackers leaked personal data of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including ICE and CBP agents. The breach exposed staff personnel records, which were subsequently published online.

news.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
news.summary: Researcher Ben Zimmermann discovered 26,400 valid credentials exposed in public Gitee repositories after scanning 7.25 million public repos. The exposed credentials were primarily API keys for cloud and AI services, representing active secrets that could be exploited by anyone accessing the public code.

news.title: Hackers Publish Work Details of 41,000 Homeland Security Employees
news.summary: A hacktivist group published the work details of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including names, titles, and phone numbers. The data was reportedly extracted from a login system, raising concerns about access controls and authentication security within federal identity infrastructure.

news.title: Session security, token protection, continuous access evaluation, and measuring what users ACTUALLY sign in with
news.summary: This article is part of a series on Microsoft Entra ID covering session security, token protection, and continuous access evaluation in the context of passkey adoption. It examines how Entra ID manages tokens post-authentication and how organizations can measure actual user sign-in methods.

news.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — and Fraudsters Are Counting on It
news.summary: The article covers social engineering attacks targeting help desks, where threat actors use AI-assisted techniques to bypass authentication and gain access by impersonating legitimate users. This directly relates to identity verification, authentication processes, and access management controls at organizational help desks.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch fixing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. The company attributed the increased vulnerability discovery rate to AI-assisted security research, while experts note organizations are struggling to keep up with patch prioritization and deployment.
